# ethereum-optimism/optimism Weekly Report (Jun 7 - 13, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week marked a major milestone in the OP Stack's architectural evolution with the successful completion of the `op-program` decoupling from the monorepo, signaling a full transition toward `rust/kona` for fault proofs. Development heavily prioritized the `op-reth` ecosystem, introducing new testing infrastructure and refining interoperability filters for the Superchain. Significant progress was also made on the `op-geth` decoupling plan, with the centralization of core chain configurations and fee logic into the new `op-core` package.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Monorepo Streamlining & `op-program` Deprecation
The long-standing initiative to decouple `op-program` reached completion this week. This effort streamlines the codebase and shifts the focus toward Rust-based implementations.
*   **Full Removal:** The `op-program` directory was deleted from the monorepo, and its references were removed from `op-e2e` and Docker images ([#21271](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21271), [#21285](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21285)).
*   **Challenger Updates:** `op-challenger` was updated to no longer require a Cannon server for permissioned games, as they do not utilize the legacy program ([#21270](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21270)).
*   **Documentation:** Operator guides were updated to refocus on `kona-client` for prestate tutorials, archiving legacy `op-program` content ([#21000](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21000)).

### `op-reth` & Execution Layer Enhancements
Significant work was dedicated to making `op-reth` the primary execution engine for the OP Stack.
*   **Testing Infrastructure:** Introduced an ephemeral, OP-flavored execution layer for the `op-reth-test-engine`, allowing for in-process testing without an embedded `op-geth` instance ([#21216](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21216)).
*   **Gas Enforcement:** Block gas limits derived from `SystemConfig` are now strictly enforced against pre-refund EVM gas under SDM/PostExec, fixing previous accounting inaccuracies ([#21250](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21250)).
*   **CLI & API:** Improved `op-proofs` CLI ergonomics and exposed a public API for the `op-reth` transaction pool ([#21277](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21277), [#21305](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21305)).

### Interoperability & Cross-Chain Messaging
The team advanced the Superchain's interoperability layer with new validation tools and monitoring alignment.
*   **Quorum Validation:** `op-reth` now supports multi-endpoint quorum validation for interop filters, fanning out requests to ensure data consistency ([#21195](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21195)).
*   **Smoke-Testing CLI:** A new tool in `op-chain-ops` allows for real-time smoke-testing of cross-chain messages, including ETH bridging roundtrips ([#21262](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21262)).
*   **Topology Alignment:** `op-interop-mon` was updated to align with the post-supervisor interop topology ([#21283](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21283)).

### Core Infrastructure & Protocol Security
*   **`op-core` Package:** Created `op-core/params` and `op-core/fees` to centralize chain configurations and L1 cost/operator-fee math, facilitating the decoupling from `go-ethereum` ([#21287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21287), [#21314](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21314)).
*   **Kona Host Resilience:** Improved witness fetching to retry via the `get_preimage` loop, addressing errors in optimistic-block re-execution ([#21269](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21269)).
*   **Process Management:** Fixed a bug in `op-challenger` to ensure VM process groups are reliably terminated on timeout ([#21268](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21268)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **`op-program` Decoupling:** Successfully closed the primary tracking issue for removing `op-program` from the monorepo ([#20276](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20276)).
*   **EIP-1559 Validation:** Resolved issues with zero elasticity decoding by pushing validation into `op-alloy` ([#18951](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18951)).
*   **SDM Refund Limits:** Implemented a protocol-level upper bound for sequencer rebates to cap maximum computation ([#20709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20709)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **SDM Devnet Rollout:** A new initiative is underway to deploy an alpha/beta devnet for the Superchain Data Model (SDM) to perform baseline benchmarks ([#21273](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21273)).
*   **Fee Math Refinement:** Active discussion continues regarding `op-core/fees`, specifically ensuring `TxRollupCostData` uses binary marshaling to avoid undercounting DA costs ([#20261](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20261)).
*   **Geth Decoupling:** Further steps have been identified to migrate `op-chain-ops/genesis` to build against upstream `go-ethereum` ([#21281](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21281)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week saw heavy collaboration on protocol-level specifications, particularly around Upgrade 19 and the Osaka-on-L2 alignment. There was significant cross-component coordination to ensure EVM hardfork resolution remains consistent across `kona-client`, `op-revm`, and `alloy-op-evm`. The introduction of a CI configuration review agent ([#21246](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21246)) indicates an ongoing effort to automate and improve the contributor experience for infrastructure changes. Additionally, the team is actively incorporating audit findings into the interop L2 contracts ([#21306](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21306)).
